sizes.text: all pictures are 256 x 256; a power of two, which game engines like.

seam_colour.text: colour: tiling seam ratio 11.24 (1.0 means no seam), peak 12.66. A visible seam: the picture does not wrap. Make the pattern tile at the source (see the guide) instead of fixing the picture afterwards.

seam_normal.text: normal: tiling seam ratio 0.85 (1.0 means no seam), peak 0.99. The left edge continues into the right edge and the top into the bottom.

seam_height.text: height: tiling seam ratio 0.77 (1.0 means no seam), peak 0.85. The left edge continues into the right edge and the top into the bottom.

seam_roughness.text: roughness: tiling seam ratio 1.06 (1.0 means no seam), peak 1.00. The left edge continues into the right edge and the top into the bottom.

seam_metallic.text: metallic: tiling seam ratio 0.30 (1.0 means no seam), peak 0.00. The left edge continues into the right edge and the top into the bottom.

seam_ao.text: ao: tiling seam ratio 0.00 (1.0 means no seam), peak 0.00. The left edge continues into the right edge and the top into the bottom.

colour_clipped.text: colour: only 0.0% pure black and 0.0% pure white pixels (no clipping).

colour_brightness.text: colour: average brightness 0.43 (0 = black, 1 = white). Surfaces in the real world sit roughly between 0.1 and 0.7; check by eye that it is not lit by a lamp or shadowed.

bits_normal.text: normal: saved with 16 bits per channel.

normal_length.text: normal: the arrows have length 1.000 (should be 1.0).

normal_mean.text: normal: the average colour is (np.float64(0.5), np.float64(0.5), np.float64(0.999)), the flat-surface blue-violet (0.5, 0.5, 1.0) as it should be.

normal_tilt.text: normal: tilt of the surface arrows is 2.8 degrees in the middle and 7.3 degrees at the 99th percentile.

normal_convention.text: normal: green points DOWN the picture = DirectX (map-alone score 0.82). Blender expects OpenGL: flip the green channel (1 minus green), or set the Normal Map node Convention to DirectX.

normal_vs_height.text: normal: agrees with the height map (DirectX); green follows the height slope with correlation -0.88, red with -0.89.

normal_strength.text: normal: the Sobel strength that would rebuild this normal map from the height is about 1.1 per pixel step (height 0..1).

bits_height.text: height: only 8 bits per channel (256 levels). Smooth slopes get stair steps in the normal map and in real displacement. Save height maps with 16 bits.

height_range.text: height: uses 0.00 to 1.00 of the 0 to 1 range.

height_clipped.text: height: 9.7% of the pixels are exactly black and 8.1% exactly white. Flat clipped plateaus lose detail.

height_levels.text: height: 256 different grey levels; 20% of neighbouring pixels exactly equal (flat areas).

roughness_note.text: roughness: remember it is DATA. In Blender the Image Texture node must be set to Non-Color; if a baked roughness looks much lighter than it should (average 0.5 turned into 0.74), it was baked into an sRGB image.

metallic_fraction.text: metallic: no metal anywhere (all black). That is correct for stone, wood, brick.

ao_range.text: ao: the picture is plain white. Ambient occlusion cannot see a Bump node or a normal map; it needs real geometry (displaced mesh, high-poly).

colour_height_link.text: colour and height agree with correlation +0.02 (stone, brick and rust usually sit between +0.3 and +0.99: darker is lower).
